text: Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a013
text: Nessa takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).

text: Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gathers Fina, Roan to talk.

speaker: a013
text: Pile's gone and I'm sitting on eleven, which is more than I'd like anyone to count for long — Fina, you're at fifteen and that number draws eyes, so I need to know if you've had anyone approach you yet this morning. Roan, Bram took two and said nothing to me beforehand, and that's new.

speaker: a010
text: Nobody's come to me yet, but fifteen food makes a man a target and I know it — I took two from the pile and kept quiet because anything more would've been a declaration. Fina, don't let anyone count your food twice in one morning, and if Mako comes near you without Nessa beside him, come find me first.

speaker: a013
text: Fina, I need to hear from your own mouth whether anyone's come to you — because fifteen is a number that doesn't stay quiet, and if Bram's already counted it, his silence to me this morning means something I don't like. Roan, the fact that Bram took two without a word and didn't look my way is either him pulling back from me or him deciding he doesn't need to explain himself anymore, and I'm not sure which one worries me more.

speaker: a015
text: Nobody's come to me yet, Nessa, and I've kept my face easy all morning — but fifteen is fifteen and I feel it the same way you do. Bram going quiet after months of feeding us both is the part that won't sit still for me: a man who gave that much food and then goes silent on pile day isn't stepping back, he's deciding. Roan, if Bram comes to you before he comes to me, I need to know what he asks first — whether it's what I have or whether it's what I'd do if someone else moved against him.

speaker: a013
text: Fina's right that Bram's deciding something — a man doesn't feed two people all year and then go quiet on pile day without a reason, and the reason I keep landing on is that he's waiting to see who comes to him first. So none of us go to him. We let him carry that silence until it gets heavy enough that he has to put it down himself, and then we'll know what it's made of.

speaker: a010
text: Nessa's read on Bram is the right one — let him carry it. What I want said in this room before we scatter is that Fina's fifteen and my two need to stay in two separate stories today, because a man counting food in this village is going to count mine first and reach hers second, and that gap is worth something if we're careful.

speaker: a013
text: Roan's right that separate stories buy us time, but the story about my eleven is already out there and anyone who watched the pile this morning can do the arithmetic — so I want us to decide right now what we say if someone asks directly, because a hesitation is the same as a confession.

speaker: a015
text: If anyone asks me directly, I'm keeping it simple — I've been holding careful all year and the pile was lean, nothing more to say than that. Nessa, your eleven is the bigger number to explain because people watched you take three from the pile on top of whatever you came in with; if someone does the count, we let them get it wrong before we correct them. And Roan's right that your two and my fifteen need to look like two separate households — don't walk close to me today.

speaker: a013
text: Fina, "let them get it wrong" only works if we all get it wrong the same way — so say it plain: if anyone pins you with a number, what's the number you give them?

speaker: a010
text: If anyone asks me flat, I tell them I came into the year with a little and took two from the pile — I don't volunteer a number. Fina, pick something low and hold it, and we both hold the same shape of answer: careful, not empty, nothing that invites a second question.

speaker: a013
text: Fina, I need that number from your mouth before we walk out of here — "something low" isn't something I can hold to if Kael or Mako catches me mid-sentence, so pick it and say it now, and I'll carry the same one.

speaker: a015
text: Eight. If anyone catches me mid-step and asks flat, I came into the year with six and took two — I've got eight, I'm fine, nothing to see. That's the number; hold it and don't blink.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Sela, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a014
text: Pile's gone before I got to it and I'm sitting on one food — Nessa, you gave me one this morning and I haven't forgotten it, but I need to know what you two are holding before I figure out whether I'm going to eat this year or not.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn, I've got five — I'll give you two right now, before anyone asks where it went. Nessa, tell me your number and we sort the rest after.

speaker: a014
text: Sela, hold the two until I hear Nessa — I want the full count before anything moves hands.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, you took three from the pile and gave one to Zinn already — I need to hear the number you're sitting on now, because Zinn's at one and I won't move food around blind when my youngest daughter might go short this year.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, I'm not asking to take from you — I'm asking so I know the shape of what we've got before I decide whether Sela needs to spend her five on me or whether we can stretch it different.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, I've been patient and Zinn's been patient, but one food won't carry her through the year and I need your number in the next breath — not because I'm counting against you, but because you're the only one in this circle who hasn't spoken it yet and that silence is starting to feel like a wall where there shouldn't be one.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, Sela's right and so am I — you've fed me twice without being asked and I don't forget that, but I'm sitting on one food with a whole year ahead and I need your number the same way you needed mine every time you asked. Say it plain and we move on.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, Zinn and I are both watching you and waiting, and the only thing your silence is telling me right now is that you're holding more than you want to say — which means you're counting something we don't know about yet. I'm your mother and I'm not going to punish you for having food, but I need the number because Zinn has one and I have five and the math between us isn't settled until I know yours.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, I've asked three times and Sela's asked twice — if you won't say it, I'm going to assume the number's high enough that you're not worried about eating, which means Sela's five can stay in her hands and I'll find another way. Don't make me guess what I should already know from my own sister.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, I'm done asking. You've got Fina to feed and that's a real weight — but Zinn has one food and she's your blood the same as Fina is, so if you're sitting on something and you're choosing not to say it to your sister's face, that's a choice I'll remember longer than you want me to.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, eleven food — that's what the village can see on you right now, same as I can. Say the number or don't, but you're not hiding it from me.

speaker: a007
text: Eleven food and silence — Nessa, I love you, but that combination tells me you've already decided something without telling us what it is, and I need you to understand that Zinn is going to eat this year whether you speak or not, because I'm giving her two of my five right now. What I want from you isn't the food — it's the reason you went quiet in front of your sister and your mother.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Ryn, Roan, Nessa, Zinn, Fina to talk.

speaker: a002
text: Taric's dead and the pile's gone again and we're twelve people now, which means what I'm about to say matters more than it did last year: Mako's sitting on four food, Ryn's got nine, Fina's got fifteen, and Nessa's got eleven — and if Bram and I are the only ones in this room with our eyes open, we're going to have a very short year. I want to know right now who in this room is still counting Mako as the shape this village is growing into, because with Taric gone, I don't have the patience to spend another year circling the same question.

speaker: a015
text: Vela just told the whole room my food count, and now everyone in this circle knows I'm carrying fifteen — that's the thing I'm sitting with right now, not Mako.

speaker: a010
text: Fina, Vela counting your food out loud in a closed room isn't the same as Mako counting it in the open — every person here already had eyes, and what Vela bought us by naming it is that nobody in this circle can pretend they didn't know. The question I want answered is whether Mako knows, because he wasn't in this room.

speaker: a003
text: Mako's got eyes the same as the rest of us — he counted Fina's food the moment the year turned, same as I did, same as you did. The room isn't the thing protecting her; what protects her is whether we move before he decides she's worth the trouble.

speaker: a015
text: Then we're already past the question of whether Mako knows — and Esa's right that the protection isn't in this room, it's in what this room decides to do. So I want to hear it said plainly: is everyone here willing to stand against Mako if he moves, the same way we stood against Bram, or are some of you going to wait and see which side looks safer when it starts?

speaker: a002
text: I'll stand when Mako moves — I've been saying it for two years and I'm done saying it, so let that be the last time anyone asks me. What I want from everyone in this room is the same thing I'm giving: not a promise to think about it, a promise to move before the arithmetic runs out. Fina, that means you too — fifteen food makes you a target, and a target who hesitates when the moment comes is worse than no ally at all.

speaker: a010
text: I'll stand when Mako moves — that's said and I won't unsay it. But I want to hear Bram say it in this room today, because last year he made that promise to Vela and Taric and me with fewer witnesses, and a promise that's only been spoken once hasn't been tested yet.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, Roan's asking the right thing and I'll name why it matters more this year than last: Taric's the one who held you to your word before, and Taric's gone, so the promise you made in that room needs to be remade in this one where everyone who's left can hear it.

speaker: a002
text: Bram, the room's been patient and I won't add another layer of asking — but I want everyone here to hear me say that I've been feeding this man for three years because I believed that word he gave last year, and if he says it again now, in front of seven witnesses instead of three, that's a debt I'll keep paying.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, I'll say it plain so you don't have to carry it alone: I've got thirty-three strength and I know what that number is worth in a fight, but I'll be standing next to you when Mako moves and that matters more than my arm. Say the word in this room and let's close.

speaker: a015
text: Bram, every person in this room has named what they'll do — the only name missing is yours, and a man who takes food and gives food and makes deals and stays quiet exactly when the room needs him to speak is a man I'm going to start counting differently than I have been.

speaker: a010
text: Bram, Fina's right and I've said my part already — so I'll say just this once more and then I'm done pressing: you stood with Nessa and fed her all year, which means you're already past the line in everything that matters, and the word this room needs is a short one.

speaker: a001
text: When Mako moves, I stand with this circle — that's the word, and it's the same one I gave last year, and it'll be the same one I give next year if I have to. Fina, Nessa — that's the reason I'm in this room, not the politics.

speaker: a002
text: Bram's word is down and I'll hold him to it the same way Taric would have — which means now I want to hear from Ryn and Zinn, because they're in this room and they've been quiet through every name that's been spoken. Ryn, you've got nine food and enough strength that Mako's first calculation includes you; where you stand is not a small thing.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn, I'll add the plain thing Vela left off the end: Dell feeds you every year, and Dell's quiet in the same direction Mako is — so when you answer Vela's question, answer both halves of it.

speaker: a002
text: Ryn, I'll say the thing Esa's pointing at without the softening: if Dell and Mako are moving in the same direction, and you're eating Dell's food, then you're already inside whatever that circle is whether you've named it or not — so tell this room now, before the question answers itself. Zinn, that goes for you too; you're Mako's blood and I won't pretend that's nothing, but blood isn't the same as a choice, and this room is offering you the chance to make one.

speaker: a009
text: Vela, I'll answer both halves because you asked plainly: I stand with this circle against Mako if he moves, same as I stood with it against Bram — and Dell is my blood, not my leash, and if you're asking whether her choices pull mine, you haven't been watching as closely as you think. What I want said before we close is that "quiet in the same direction" is not the same as a choice, and I'll have that conversation with Dell myself before anyone in this room decides what her silence means.

speaker: a003
text: Zinn, Ryn's spoken and I'll hold her to it — but you're the name that's still unspoken, and you're Mako's blood and Sela's daughter and I'm not going to pretend that's simple, so I'm asking you directly: when Mako moves, where do you stand?

speaker: a001
text: Zinn's the one this room is waiting on, not me — I've said my word and I'll hold it. But I want to name something while we're all here: Ryn just told us she'll talk to Dell, and Dell's been moving food to Ryn for years, which means that conversation either brings Dell into this circle or it tells us something we need to know before Mako moves. I'd rather know Dell's answer now than find out she's standing on the wrong side when it counts.

speaker: a009
text: Bram's right that we need Dell's answer, but I want to be plain about something this room is dancing around: Dell has eleven food and eighty-five strength, and if she's standing with Mako when he moves, the arithmetic in this room changes fast — so when I go to her, I'm not just asking where she stands, I'm offering her a reason to stand here instead.

speaker: a001
text: Ryn, go to Dell today, not tomorrow — and when you do, don't frame it as a choice between us and Mako, frame it as math: fifteen food on Fina's back is a number Dell can count as easily as anyone, and a woman with eighty-five strength knows what it means to be the one who decides which way that goes. Bring her answer back before the day turns.

speaker: a003
text: Zinn, we're still waiting on your name — Bram's got his word out, Ryn's walking to Dell before dark, and the only silence left in this room is yours. I know Mako's your father and I'm not asking you to hate him, I'm asking you to decide who you're protecting when it matters.

speaker: a009
text: Zinn, I'll say one thing to make the room easier for you: no one here is asking you to stand against your father's blood, we're asking you to stand with Nessa — and you've been feeding Nessa all year, so the truth is you've already been making this choice, you just haven't named it yet.

speaker: a001
text: Zinn's been feeding Nessa all year and that's a fact this room already knew — what I want from her is the word, same as the room wanted it from me, because a choice that's only lived in food and not in words is a choice that bends when her father's in the room asking her to remember whose blood she came from.

speaker: a002
text: Zinn, I've watched you feed Nessa from the moment you were born into this village, and I won't pretend I don't know why — so I'll say the thing nobody else has said plainly: if Mako moves on Fina's food, Nessa's in the middle of that, and you can't protect her from both sides at once. Say the word, and you're not choosing against your father, you're choosing for your sister.

speaker: a001
text: Zinn, the word's the only thing missing — everything else you've already given.

speaker: a009
text: Zinn, I've been watching you hold your tongue through every name this room has spoken, and I'll tell you what I told Dell when Dav's loyalties were in question: the longer you stay silent, the more the room fills in the answer for you, and you won't like what they write. You've been choosing Nessa with your hands all year — say it with your mouth and let this room close.

speaker: a001
text: Zinn, I've got two food and fifty-eight strength and I'm the smallest number in this circle — but I'm Nessa's father and I'll be standing when Mako moves, and that means I need to know you're standing too before I walk out of this room. If you won't say it for the circle, say it for her.

speaker: a009
text: Zinn, I've said everything I have to say to this room and I meant every word of it — but you're the last door standing open, and if you walk out of here without naming where you stand, I'm going to have to carry that back to Dell and tell her the circle isn't as solid as I promised it was.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Zinn to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Zinn, pile's gone and you're sitting on one food — that's too thin for a year that's already started dry. How much did Nessa give you before the pile ran out, and is she going to keep coming?

speaker: a007
text: Sela gives 2 food to Zinn.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Ryn, pile's empty and I've got three food — tell me your number before anything else, because the year's already running and I won't let last year's pattern repeat where you end up thin while I'm still counting.

speaker: a009
text: Nine food, Dell — I'm standing better than last year. I need to tell you something before the day gets louder: Vela's circle is asking where you stand, and they asked me to answer for you, and I told them I'd bring the question to you myself. Where are you?

speaker: a011
text: With us — same answer I've had since year one, and Vela knows it even if she needed to hear it said out loud. Tell me what she's actually asking, because "where do you stand" from Vela in a year where Bram's still breathing and Taric just starved isn't small talk, it's a shape I need to see before I agree to walk inside it.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Zinn.

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Esa, Roan to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, Roan — the pile's gone and I've got two food in hand, same as Roan, and the thing I want said between us before anyone else starts talking is this: Taric's dead and that leaves Esa alone, which is the kind of thing a man like Bram notices before we do. I'm asking plainly whether either of you needs food to stay fed through the year, because I'd rather give it now than watch another person in this circle starve.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Vela's been feeding Bram for two years running — food straight from her hand to his — and now she's asking where I stand, which means either she's woken up to what she's been doing or she's asking on his behalf, and I need to know which before I let her count me in her circle.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Ryn, you're the one she came to, which means she reads you as the door to me — so I want to know how she sounded when she asked: did she sound like a woman who's finally counting the cost of what she's been handing Bram, or did she sound like a woman running an errand for someone else?

speaker: a008
text: Nessa gave me two this morning and Sela came right after with two more — I'm at six now, so the thin spell didn't last. What worries me more is Fina: she's sitting on seventeen and hasn't moved a single piece of it toward anyone but Roan, and that much food in one hand draws eyes.

speaker: a003
text: Esa gives 1 food to Bram.

speaker: a001

speaker: a008

speaker: a008
text: Seventeen in one hand is a target whether Fina knows it or not, and Roan's the only one she's feeding — that's a small circle for a woman holding that much weight. If someone moves on her, we want to be close enough that she remembers we didn't, not close enough that we're in the middle of it.

speaker: a003

speaker: a001

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Esa, Roan to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, I watched you give food to Bram twice just now, and I need you to tell me what that is — because if you're buying protection from him, I understand it, but I need to know, and if you're doing it for some other reason, I need to know that too.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a011
text: She sounded like a woman who's finally counting the cost — there was something tired in it, not the way a messenger sounds, but the way someone sounds when they've been watching a hole in their food sack get bigger and they finally looked down to see how much is gone. I think she's waking up. But I'd want to hear her say Bram's name herself before I trust that she's done feeding him.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Then let's find out — I want to talk to Vela directly, and I want you beside me when I do, because a woman who's waking up needs to see what she's waking up toward, not just hear about it from a distance. If she says Bram's name without being asked, we bring her in. If she doesn't, we're polite and we learn something useful either way.

speaker: a008
text: Fina's young and she's never seen a year where the pile runs dry before half the village gets to it — she doesn't know yet that seventeen is a debt she owes to everyone watching. I'm going to find a reason to pass near her today, nothing that looks like approach, just enough that she knows my face isn't a threat. If she's smart, she'll start spreading before someone makes the decision for her.

speaker: a008
text: Zinn's feeding Nessa again — I watched her give twice in the last stretch, and Nessa's got eleven still, so that's not charity, that's a loop that's been running since before Eron died. You've been in that loop longer than anyone; if Fina starts looking to spread, Nessa's the door she'll come through, not me.

text: Kael gathers Esa, Roan to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, I'm still waiting on that answer, and the longer you stay quiet the more I'm reading it myself — so tell me plain, because the three of us need to be counting the same things right now or we're not a circle, we're just three people standing near each other.

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Esa, Roan to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, you've given Bram three food now and he's handed every piece of it straight to Nessa — which tells me exactly what he told you, that feeding his daughter keeps you safe, and I've sat with that long enough to say: I understand the logic, but you're building his household while yours has a hole in it where Taric used to stand, and that's a trade that only runs one direction.
